context: Research current upstream artifact signing and Homebrew status; compare clickhousectl, official direct binary installation, and Docker against reproducibility, Gatekeeper compatibility, version pinning, Apple Silicon support, and BenchBox test/CI needs; then implement the narrowest supported documentation or automation change.
description: Future concern: Homebrew deprecated the clickhouse cask because the upstream macOS binary fails the macOS Gatekeeper check; the cask is scheduled to be disabled on 2026-09-01. The current cask downloads ClickHouse release binaries and the upgrade to 26.7.1.1315-stable completed successfully, so this is not an immediate outage. Findings: ClickHouse Inc. is the commercial company and also maintains the Apache-2.0 ClickHouse OSS project; clickhouse.com is therefore an official OSS distribution channel, not only ClickHouse Cloud. The historical Altinity/homebrew-clickhouse tap redirects to ClickHouse/homebrew-clickhouse, is explicitly deprecated/unused, says no future fixes will be made, and its latest release is 23.5.3.24 from 2023-06-30. A tap-only change cannot make an upstream executable pass Gatekeeper; a community rebuild/signing pipeline would be a separate distribution with release and trust obligations. Proposed actions: before the disable date, verify whether ClickHouse publishes signed/notarized macOS artifacts; choose and document a supported BenchBox developer/CI path, likely clickhousectl or the official installer for local development and Docker for reproducible server testing; assess version pinning, Apple Silicon behavior, upgrade/data compatibility, and test coverage; update BenchBox setup documentation and automation if needed. Do not adopt the stale Altinity tap as the default replacement.
